01
Head Rotation
NeckMobility5 each direction

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and shoulders relaxed.
2
Tilt your chin toward your chest, then roll one ear toward the same-side shoulder.
3
Draw a slow half-circle across the front of the body to the other shoulder, without tipping the head back.
4
Do 5 slow half-circles in each direction.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Move slowly and smoothly — the neck needs a gentle warm-up.
📌Keep the shoulders down and relaxed throughout.
⚠️Skip any position that pinches or makes you dizzy.
💡 Pro TipKeep the range small and easy — this is a warm-up, not a stretch.
02
Shoulder Rotation
ShouldersRotator Cuff10 each direction

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Stand tall with arms relaxed at your sides.
2
Roll both shoulders forward in big, smooth circles for 10 reps.
3
Reverse the direction and roll backward for 10 reps.
4
Finish with 10 full arm circles each way, starting small and getting bigger.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Pull the shoulders down away from your ears on every circle.
📌Use the full range of motion, smooth and controlled.
⚠️Stop if you feel a pinch at the front of the shoulder.
💡 Pro TipBig circles lubricate the joint before pressing and pulling.
03
Wrist Rotation
WristsForearms10 each direction

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Extend your arms in front of you or clasp your hands together.
2
Rotate both wrists in slow circles for 10 reps clockwise.
3
Reverse to counter-clockwise for 10 reps.
4
Finish by opening and closing your fists 10 times.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Keep the forearms still — only the wrists move.
📌Make each circle as full and smooth as possible.
⚠️Stay gentle; never force the end range.
💡 Pro TipWrists take load in presses, curls and pulls — never skip them.
04
Hip Rotation
HipsLower Back10 each direction

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulders and hands on your hips.
2
Draw large circles with your hips, like using a hula hoop.
3
Do 10 circles clockwise, then 10 counter-clockwise.
4
Keep the knees soft and the shoulders stacked over the hips.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Move from the hips, not the knees or shoulders.
📌Make the circles wide and smooth.
⚠️Keep the movement controlled — no jerking.
💡 Pro TipLoose hips make squats, lunges and deadlifts feel smoother.
05
Knee Rotation
KneesJoint Prep10 each direction

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Stand with feet together and bend slightly at the knees, hands resting on your kneecaps.
2
Rotate both knees in small, slow circles for 10 reps clockwise.
3
Reverse for 10 reps counter-clockwise.
4
Keep the movement small and comfortable.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Keep the circles small and slow.
📌Hands rest lightly on the knees for support.
⚠️Stop if you feel sharp pain rather than easy movement.
💡 Pro TipThis only wakes up the joint — keep it light.
06
Ankle Rotation
AnklesCalves10 each direction

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Stand on one leg, holding a wall or support if needed, with the other toe resting lightly on the floor.
2
Rotate the ankle in slow, full circles for 10 reps clockwise.
3
Reverse for 10 reps counter-clockwise.
4
Switch legs and repeat.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Draw the biggest circle you can with the toes.
📌Keep the shin still so only the ankle moves.
⚠️Use a wall or rack if your balance wobbles.
💡 Pro TipMobile ankles help you reach squat depth with good form.
07
Leg Swings
HamstringsHip Flexors10 per leg

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Hold a rack or wall for balance and stand tall on one leg.
2
Swing the other leg forward and backward in a controlled arc.
3
Build the range gradually over 10 swings, keeping the torso still.
4
Switch legs, then optionally repeat swinging side to side across the body.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Stay tall — do not lean with the swing.
📌Start small and increase the range with each swing.
⚠️Swing under control; no yanking the leg.
💡 Pro TipLoosens hips and hamstrings before squats, deadlifts and lunges.
08
Open and Close the Gate
Hip RotatorsGlutesAdductors10 per leg

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Stand tall, holding a rack or wall for balance, and lift one knee up in front of you to hip height.
2
Open the gate: rotate the knee outward to the side, then lower the foot to the floor beside you.
3
Close the gate: lift the leg out to the side with the knee bent, rotate the knee forward and across the front of your body, then lower the foot.
4
Do 10 open and 10 close reps on each leg.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Keep the standing leg stable and the torso upright.
📌Make each circle smooth and use the full range of the hip.
⚠️Hold a support if balance is an issue and avoid swinging the leg.
💡 Pro TipOpen and close the gate on the same leg so the hip warms up in both directions.
09
Hamstring Scoops
HamstringsGlutes10 reps

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Step one leg forward with the heel on the floor and toes up, the other knee slightly bent.
2
Hinge at the hips with a flat back and reach both hands down toward the front foot.
3
Scoop your hands back along the floor toward the body as you stand tall and reach overhead.
4
Alternate legs for 10 total reps.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Push the hips back — this is a hinge, not a squat.
📌Keep the back flat and the chest proud.
⚠️Do not round the lower back to reach further.
💡 Pro TipA great primer for Deadlift and Romanian Deadlift days.
10
Quad Pull
QuadsHip Flexors20 sec per leg

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Stand tall, holding a wall or rack for balance if needed.
2
Bend one knee and pull the heel toward your glute, holding the ankle.
3
Keep the knees together and tuck the pelvis slightly forward.
4
Hold about 20 seconds, then switch legs.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Keep the knees side by side and hips squared.
📌Squeeze the glute of the working leg for a deeper stretch.
⚠️Do not arch the lower back to pull the foot higher.
💡 Pro TipA short hold is enough — you are warming up, not stretching deeply.
11
Bodyweight Squats
QuadsGlutes15 reps

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out and chest tall.
2
Sit your hips back and down until the thighs are roughly parallel to the floor.
3
Keep the knees tracking over the toes and the heels on the floor.
4
Drive up through the heels. Complete 15 smooth reps.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Chest up and core braced the whole way down.
📌Knees push out in line with the toes.
⚠️Do not let the heels lift or the knees cave inward.
💡 Pro TipUse this to groove your squat pattern before loaded sets.
12
Calf Raise
CalvesAnkles15 reps

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, holding a support if needed.
2
Rise onto your toes as high as you can.
3
Pause briefly at the top.
4
Lower slowly and repeat for 15 reps.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Push through the big toe and keep the ankles straight.
📌Pause at the top for a full contraction.
⚠️Do not bounce — move with control.
💡 Pro TipWarms up the calves and ankles ahead of jumps and heavy leg work.
13
Jumping Jacks
Full BodyCardio30–45 sec

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Stand tall with feet together, arms at your sides.
2
Jump feet outward wider than shoulder-width while raising both arms overhead simultaneously.
3
Jump feet back together and lower arms back to your sides in one smooth motion.
4
Maintain a consistent rhythm. Core braced. Land softly with knees slightly bent.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Land softly on the balls of your feet to keep joint impact low.
📌Raises heart rate and body temperature before lifting.
⚠️Keep a steady, rhythmic pace rather than rushing the reps.
💡 Pro TipClassic full-body warm-up — loosens the shoulders and hips while elevating heart rate before your session.
14
High Knees
CardioHip Flexors30 sec

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and arms ready to move naturally.
2
Jog in place while driving one knee up toward hip height, then quickly switch sides.
3
Pump your arms like a sprint and stay light on the balls of your feet.
4
Keep the pace quick but controlled, staying upright through the torso.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Lift knees with the core engaged, not by leaning back.
📌Stay light and fast off the floor for better rhythm and conditioning.
⚠️Do not stomp the feet — land softly to reduce joint stress.
💡 Pro TipGreat dynamic warm-up to wake up the hip flexors, core, and heart rate before lifting.
15
Pogo Jumps
PlyometricCalves20 hops

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Stand tall with feet about hip-width apart and knees softly unlocked.
2
Perform quick, springy vertical hops using mostly the ankles and calves.
3
Keep the torso stacked, arms relaxed, and ground contact very short.
4
Land softly and immediately rebound into the next jump with rhythm.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Think “stiff ankles, soft landing” for clean elastic rebounds.
📌These are small, reactive jumps — height is less important than bounce quality.
⚠️If Achilles or calves feel overloaded, shorten the set and reduce jump height.
💡 Pro TipExcellent for developing lower-leg stiffness and reactive conditioning when done in short sets.

01
Flat Bench Press Barbell / Dumbbell
ChestTricepsFront Delt

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Lie flat on the bench with feet planted shoulder-width on the floor and shoulder blades retracted and depressed.
2
Grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width, or hold dumbbells at chest level with palms facing forward.
3
Lower slowly (3 sec) to mid-chest under full control with elbows angled 45–70° from your torso.
4
Press explosively upward and squeeze the chest hard at the top.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Keep chest proud with shoulder blades pinched tight into the bench.
📌Elbows stay 45–70° from the torso — never flared straight out to 90°.
⚠️Never bounce the weight off your chest — control every inch of the descent.
💡 Pro TipBarbell lets you overload heavier; dumbbells allow a deeper stretch and freer wrist angle.
02
Incline Dumbbell / Machine Press
Upper ChestFront DeltTriceps

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Set an incline bench to ~30° (or adjust the incline press machine so handles align with your upper chest). Plant feet flat and retract shoulder blades.
2
Hold dumbbells at upper-chest level with elbows angled ~45–60° from your torso, or grip the machine handles overhand.
3
Press smoothly upward until arms are nearly extended over your shoulders, squeezing the upper chest hard at the top.
4
Lower slowly over 3 seconds into a deep, controlled upper-chest stretch before the next rep.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌30° incline targets the upper chest best — steeper angles shift too much load onto the front delts.
📌Keep shoulder blades pinched into the pad and chest proud throughout the set.
⚠️Avoid flaring elbows wide to 90° or bouncing out of the bottom stretch.
💡 Pro TipPairs with Day 4 Incline Press for 2×/week upper-chest growth — dumbbells maximize stretch, while the machine lets you push safely near failure.
03
Shoulder Press Machine / Dumbbell
All Delt HeadsTriceps

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Sit upright with back support; grip the shoulder press machine handles or hold dumbbells at shoulder height.
2
Start with elbows bent around 90°, core braced, and feet planted flat on the floor.
3
Press smoothly overhead until arms are nearly straight without snapping the elbows locked.
4
Lower slowly over 3 seconds back to ear/chin level to stretch the deltoids.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Keep your upper and lower back supported against the pad — do not lean back.
📌Stop just short of hard elbow lockout to keep constant tension on the delts.
⚠️Keep ribs down and core braced — avoid overarching the lower back.
💡 Pro TipPosition elbows slightly in front of your torso (scapular plane) for smoother, safer shoulder mechanics.
04
Dips / Weighted Dips
Lower ChestTriceps

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Grip parallel bars with straight arms (add a dip belt or hold a dumbbell between your feet for weighted sets).
2
Lean torso forward 20–30° for more chest activation throughout the set.
3
Lower slowly until elbows reach 90°. Feel a deep chest stretch at the bottom.
4
Push explosively back up without snapping the elbows into hard lockout at the top.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Lean forward = chest focus. Stay upright = triceps focus.
📌Keep elbows tucked comfortably — avoid flaring wide.
⚠️Stop around 90° elbow bend — dropping too deep stresses the front of the shoulder.
💡 Pro TipMaster strict, controlled bodyweight reps before adding external weight on a dip belt.
05
Pec Fly
ChestFront Delt

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Sit at the pec deck or cable station. Adjust handles to mid-chest height with arms slightly bent.
2
Grip handles and keep that slight elbow bend fixed throughout — it is a fly, not a press.
3
Bring hands together in front of your chest in a wide sweeping arc and squeeze pecs hard.
4
Return slowly with a full stretch — feel the chest open wide on every rep.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Think "hugging a barrel" — arms sweep in a wide arc, elbows don't straighten.
📌Squeeze and hold at center for 1 second — peak pec contraction.
⚠️Don't let arms go too far back — stop at chest level to protect the shoulder.
💡 Pro TipPerfect mid-chest isolation after pressing — gives your triceps a rest before close-grip bench.
06
Incline Machine Fly / Dumbbell
Upper Chest (Isolation)Front Delt

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Adjust the incline fly machine so handles align with your upper chest (or lie on a 30° incline bench with dumbbells).
2
Keep your arms slightly bent and hold that fixed arc throughout — it is a fly, not a press.
3
Bring the handles or dumbbells together above your upper chest in a sweeping arc and squeeze hard at the center.
4
Open arms back into a full, controlled stretch — feel the upper chest opening wide on every rep.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Arms stay in a fixed arc like hugging a barrel — do not straighten or press them.
📌Squeeze at the center for 1 full second — that is the peak upper-chest contraction.
⚠️Don't go too wide on the stretch — stop when you feel tension, not shoulder strain.
💡 Pro TipIsolates the clavicular upper chest without triceps involvement — great finisher for upper-chest fullness.
07
Close-Grip Barbell Bench Press
TricepsInner ChestFront Delt

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Lie on a flat bench and grip the bar slightly narrower than shoulder-width.
2
Unrack and lower the bar to your lower chest with the elbows tucked.
3
Keep the elbows close to the body throughout the movement.
4
Press the bar back up powerfully until the arms lock out.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Grip about shoulder-width — too narrow stresses the wrists.
📌Tuck the elbows to roughly 45° to load the triceps.
⚠️Keep the wrists stacked over the elbows; do not let them bend back.
💡 Pro TipOne of the best mass-builders for the triceps while still training the chest.
08
Overhead Rope Cable Extension
Triceps Long Head

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Attach rope to low cable. Stand facing away. Grip rope behind head, elbows pointing straight up.
2
Upper arms stay vertical and close to head throughout. Only forearms move — elbows are the fixed pivot.
3
Extend arms fully overhead until straight. Flare rope ends slightly at the top for full contraction.
4
Lower slowly back behind head — feel the long-head stretch at the bottom every rep.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Upper arms stay pinned vertical — they are the fixed point the whole set.
📌Cable provides constant tension unlike a dumbbell — better stretch at the bottom.
⚠️Go lighter here — the long-head stretch is intense and easy to strain.
💡 Pro TipDeeper you go = more long-head stretch. Full range of motion is where growth happens.
Treadmill / Cycling · 10,000 steps
09
Treadmill / Cycling · Walk + Incline + Jog
WalkIncline WalkJogCycling10,000 steps75 min

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Warm-up walk: 5 min at 6.0 km/h, 0% incline (about 600 steps).
2
Incline walk: 10 min at 6.0 km/h, 6% incline (about 1,200 steps).
3
Jog and walk: 5 min jog at 9.0 km/h, 1% incline, then 2 min walk at 6.0 km/h. Repeat for 6 rounds, 42 min in total (about 6,240 steps).
4
Incline walk: 10 min at 6.0 km/h, 6% incline (about 1,200 steps).
5
Slow walk: 8 min at 4.5 km/h, 0% incline (about 800 steps). Total about 10,000 steps in 75 min.
6
Cycling option: 45–60 min on a stationary bike — 5 min easy warm-up, steady moderate pace at 75–90 RPM (or intervals), and 5 min cool-down.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Keep an easy, talkable effort — you should speak in short sentences while jogging or cycling.
📌Keep the incline at 1% when jogging and do not hold the handrails; set bike saddle height so the knee keeps a slight bend at the bottom.
⚠️Shin, knee, or foot pain that builds up means switch to walking or cycling for the day.
💡 Pro TipSteps are estimates (about 120 a minute walking, 160 jogging). Check your watch or phone and lengthen or shorten the final slow walk to land on 10,000. Cannot hold 9.0 km/h yet? Jog at 8.0 km/h and add a few minutes of walking.

PULL DAY

Back · Rear Delts · Biceps

Muscle Activation Map

Primary

01
Deadlift
Lower BackHamstringsGlutesTraps

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Stand over bar, feet hip-width. Hinge at hips, grip just outside your knees.
2
Chest tall, back flat. Deep breath and brace core hard — like bracing for a punch.
3
Push floor away through heels. Bar drags close along shins as you rise up.
4
Drive hips forward to stand tall. Squeeze glutes hard at full lockout.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Chest tall, shoulders back — absolutely NO rounding of the back at any point.
📌Bar stays close to your body the entire movement — never swing it outward.
⚠️Lower-back rounding = serious injury risk. Reduce weight if it rounds at all.
💡 Pro TipThink "push the floor away" not "pull the weight up" — fires the posterior chain far better.
02
Pull-Ups / Weighted Pull-Ups
LatsBicepsMid Back

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Dead hang from bar. Hands wider than shoulders, palms facing away from you.
2
RETRACT shoulder blades FIRST before pulling with your arms at all.
3
Pull chin over bar. Chest leans slightly toward bar at the top position.
4
Lower fully to dead hang — don't cut range of motion short.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌"Pull elbows to back pockets" — fires lats far more effectively than arm-pulling.
📌Slight backward lean with chest up toward the bar as you pull upward.
⚠️Use band or machine assistance if needed to keep strict form before adding weight.
💡 Pro TipDead hangs between sets improve grip strength and shoulder health long-term.
03
Chest-Supported Row Machine / Dumbbell
Mid BackLatsRear Delts

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Set your chest firmly against an incline bench or chest-supported row pad.
2
Start with arms extended and shoulders controlled, not rounded forward aggressively.
3
Pull the handles or dumbbells toward your lower ribs while driving elbows back.
4
Squeeze the shoulder blades, then lower slowly until the back is stretched again.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Keep your chest glued to the pad; do not lift your torso to cheat.
📌Pull with elbows, not just your hands.
⚠️Avoid shrugging at the top; keep neck long and shoulders down.
💡 Pro TipGreat row variation when your lower back is tired from deadlifts or bent-over rows.
04
Seated Cable Row (2s) + Seated Row Machine (2s)
RhomboidsMid TrapsLats

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Seated Cable Row (2 sets): sit tall with feet braced on the platform and grab the V-bar or close-grip handle.
2
Pull to your lower ribs/navel while staying upright, squeeze your shoulder blades, then return with a controlled lat stretch.
3
Seated Row Machine (2 sets): brace your chest against the pad and grip the handles at mid-back height.
4
Drive elbows straight back, hold peak contraction for 1 second, and lower slowly without letting the stack slam.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Squeeze shoulder blades together hard at full contraction every rep.
📌Don't rock backward — swinging cheats reps and stresses the lower back.
⚠️Keep elbows tracking close to your sides rather than flaring high.
💡 Pro TipCable rows challenge trunk stability, while the chest-pad machine lets you isolate mid-back safely to failure.
05
Straight-Arm Pulldown / Pull Over Machine
Lats (Isolation)Serratus

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Face a high cable with a straight bar or rope (or sit strapped into a pullover machine with elbows braced on the pads).
2
On cables, step back, hinge slightly at the hips with a braced core, and keep a slight elbow bend fixed throughout.
3
Sweep the bar or machine pads down in a smooth arc to your hips using only your lats — arms do not bend further.
4
Squeeze lats hard at the bottom, then return slowly overhead to feel a full, controlled lat stretch on every rep.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Arms keep the exact same bend angle the whole movement — pure lat isolation with zero biceps help.
📌If your elbows start bending or triceps press the bar down, the weight is too heavy — reduce it.
⚠️Keep shoulders depressed away from your ears as your arms rise into the top stretch.
💡 Pro TipPlaced right after pull-ups and rows, this finishes off the lats completely without your biceps limiting the set.
06
Cable Face Pull
Rear DeltoidExternal Rotators

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Set cable at upper-chest or face height with a rope attachment. Step back to create tension.
2
Grip the rope ends with thumbs pointing back toward you and arms extended forward.
3
Pull the rope apart toward your forehead/ears while externally rotating your shoulders.
4
Finish with hands beside your ears and elbows at 90°. Squeeze rear delts for 1 second.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Crucial for shoulder health — balances all your pressing volume.
📌Finish in a "double biceps pose" — thumbs back, elbows high and wide.
⚠️Use light weight — this is precision rear-delt and rotator-cuff work, not ego lifting.
💡 Pro TipDo 3×15–20 every pull session to build rear delts and protect the rotator cuff.
07
Incline Seated Dumbbell Curl
Biceps Long HeadBiceps Short Head

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Set bench to 45–60° incline. Sit back with upper arms hanging straight down behind the bench.
2
Hold dumbbells underhand grip. Arms fully extended at bottom — feel the stretch.
3
Curl upward toward shoulders. Keep upper arms pinned vertical against the bench pad.
4
Squeeze biceps hard at top. Lower SLOWLY — the eccentric stretch drives growth.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Upper arms stay vertical and still — they are the fixed pivot point the whole set.
📌Incline angle increases stretch on the long head — builds a taller biceps peak.
⚠️Go lighter than expected — the stretched bottom position makes this much harder.
💡 Pro TipThe long head gets a full stretch at the bottom — impossible to replicate standing.
08
Hammer Dumbbell Curl (2s) + Concentration Curl (2s)
BrachialisBrachioradialisBiceps Short Head

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Hammer Curl (2 sets): stand with dumbbells at your sides, palms facing inward in a neutral grip.
2
Keep the elbows fixed and curl both dumbbells up, then lower under control for all reps.
3
Concentration Curl (2 sets): sit on a bench, brace one upper arm against your inner thigh, and let the arm hang fully extended.
4
Curl that single dumbbell up with palms supinated, squeeze the peak for 1 second, and repeat on both arms.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌The neutral hammer grip builds the brachialis; the concentration curl peaks the biceps.
📌Keep the upper arm still in both movements — no swinging or shrugging.
⚠️Control the lowering phase; don't let momentum take over as you fatigue.
💡 Pro TipPairing hammer and concentration curls hits arm thickness and the biceps peak in one superset.

01
Smith Machine Squats / Barbell Squats
QuadsGlutesHamstringsCore

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Set the bar across your upper traps (in a Smith machine or squat rack). Stand shoulder-width apart with toes turned out 15–30°.
2
Unrack, take a deep breath, and brace your core hard. Keep the bar over mid-foot on barbell squats, or set feet slightly forward on the Smith machine.
3
Sit your hips back and down until thighs reach at least parallel, keeping knees tracking over your toes.
4
Drive powerfully through your heels to stand tall and squeeze glutes at lockout.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌On the Smith machine, placing feet slightly forward keeps shins more vertical for quad focus.
📌On barbell squats, brace 360° through your core and keep chest proud throughout.
⚠️Actively push knees outward in line with toes — never let them cave inward.
💡 Pro TipBarbell squats build full-body stability, while the Smith machine lets you isolate quads safely to deeper fatigue.
02
Romanian Deadlift Barbell / Dumbbell
HamstringsGlutesLower Back

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Hold a barbell or dumbbells at hip level with feet hip-width apart and a soft bend in the knees.
2
Push your hips straight backward while keeping the weight close along your thighs and chest proud.
3
Lower to mid-shin until hamstrings are fully stretched — stop before any lower-back rounding.
4
Drive hips forward to stand tall and squeeze glutes at the top.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌RDL ≠ Squat — keep a fixed, soft knee bend while the hips do all the hinging.
📌Keep the barbell or dumbbells grazing your legs throughout the entire rep.
⚠️Stop as soon as your hips stop moving back — going lower only rounds the lumbar spine.
💡 Pro Tip3-second lowering phase = much more time under tension = significantly more hamstring growth.
03
Leg Press N (7r) + W (7r) + H (7r) + L (7r)
QuadsGlutesHamstrings

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Sit in the leg press with your lower back and hips pressed firmly against the pad, then unlock the safeties.
2
Complete 7 reps in each foot position: Narrow (outer quads) → Wide (adductors & glutes) → High (glutes & hamstrings) → Low (quads).
3
Lower the sled under control until knees reach ~90°, then drive powerfully through your heels.
4
Keep a slight bend in the knees at the top — never lock out your knees under heavy load.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌High/wide placement biases glutes & adductors; low/narrow placement biases quads.
📌Lower back and tailbone must stay glued to the seat pad at all times.
⚠️Re-rack briefly if needed when adjusting foot placement, and keep knees tracking over toes.
💡 Pro TipUse a moderate load so all 28 reps across the 4 stances stay controlled with full range of motion.
04
Leg Extension
Quadriceps (Isolation)

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Sit in machine. Adjust so knees align with the pivot point. Pad on lower shins.
2
Extend legs until almost fully straight. Squeeze quads hard at the very top.
3
Lower slowly over 3 seconds — fight gravity on the way down every rep.
4
Stop just before full flex at bottom — keep tension, never let weight rest.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Hold the side handles firmly and keep your hips planted on the seat.
📌Sit tall against the back pad — don't slouch or let hips slide forward.
⚠️Hold 1 second at the top every rep where the quads contract most fully.
💡 Pro TipBest used after squats and leg press — isolates the quads through a full peak contraction.
05
Lying Leg Curl
Hamstrings (Isolation)

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Lie face down on machine. Ankles under the pad. Hips flat on the pad.
2
Curl heels toward your glutes as far as possible. Pause at the very top.
3
Lower slowly over 3 seconds — fight gravity on the way down.
4
Don't let hips lift off the pad — if they do, weight is too heavy.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Hips stay glued to the pad — if they rise, reduce the weight immediately.
📌Keep ankles dorsiflexed (toes pulled toward shins) for stronger hamstring recruitment.
⚠️Control the 3-second lowering phase — don't let the weight stack drop.
💡 Pro TipSqueeze and hold 1 second at the top every rep — hamstrings will be on fire.
06
Barbell Calf Raise Stand (2s) + Sit (2s)
GastrocnemiusSoleus

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Standing (2 sets — Gastrocnemius): stand tall with a barbell across your upper back and balls of your feet on a plate or step, legs straight.
2
Lower heels into a full stretch, press high onto your toes, pause 1 second, and repeat for 15–20 reps.
3
Seated (2 sets — Soleus): sit on a bench with balls of your feet elevated and a padded barbell across your lower thighs (or use a seated calf machine).
4
Drop heels deep at the bottom, drive up to full tiptoe, hold 1 second, and complete 15–25 controlled reps.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Standing targets the gastrocnemius; seated (bent knee) isolates the deep soleus.
📌Push evenly through the ball of your big toe so ankles stay stacked straight.
⚠️Never bounce out of the bottom — pause 1 second at both the stretch and the peak.
💡 Pro TipCalves are stubborn — full range + high reps + progressive overload is the only real formula.
07
Tibialis Raises
Tibialis AnteriorShin StrengthAnkle Dorsiflexion

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Stand with your heels planted and your back supported against a wall or stable surface. Keep the knees slightly bent and toes pointing forward.
2
Lift the front of your feet up toward your shins as high as possible while keeping the heels on the floor.
3
Pause briefly at the top and feel the front of the lower legs working without rocking the body backward.
4
Lower the toes back down slowly under control and repeat for smooth, consistent reps.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌 Keep the heels grounded and let the movement come from the ankles, not from swinging the hips.
📌 Raise the toes evenly and maintain control through the full range instead of bouncing the reps.
⚠️ If you feel cramping in the feet, reduce speed and shorten the range slightly until control improves.
💡 Pro TipHigher-rep sets work very well here — focus on clean dorsiflexion and a short pause at the top of each rep.
Core
08
Hanging Leg Raise
Lower Abs

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Dead hang from pull-up bar. Arms straight, entire body relaxed at start.
2
Brace core hard. Raise straight legs to parallel (or higher if flexible).
3
Pause 1 second at the top — resist any swinging momentum.
4
Lower slowly with full control. Zero swinging — it defeats the purpose.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌No swinging — if momentum creeps in, start with bent-knee raises first.
📌The lowering phase is equally important — control it with full tension.
⚠️Curl your pelvis upward at the top so the lower abs work, not just the hip flexors.
💡 Pro TipProgression: bent knee raises → L-sit → straight leg raises → toes to bar.
09
Pallof Press
ObliquesAnti-Rotation CoreTransverse Abs

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Set a cable at chest height and stand sideways to the stack, feet shoulder-width apart.
2
Hold the handle with both hands at the center of your chest, core braced and ribs down.
3
Press the handle straight out until the arms are fully extended, resisting the cable’s pull to rotate you.
4
Hold 2 seconds, then bring the handle back to the chest slowly. Finish all reps, then switch sides.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Keep the hips and shoulders square to the front — do not let the cable turn you.
📌Squeeze the glutes and keep the ribs down for a stable trunk.
⚠️If the torso twists or leans, reduce the weight.
💡 Pro TipStepping farther from the stack makes it harder without adding plates.
Treadmill / Cycling · 10,000 steps
10
Treadmill / Cycling · Walk + Incline + Jog
WalkIncline WalkJogCycling10,000 steps75 min

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Warm-up walk: 5 min at 6.0 km/h, 0% incline (about 600 steps).
2
Incline walk: 10 min at 6.0 km/h, 6% incline (about 1,200 steps).
3
Jog and walk: 5 min jog at 9.0 km/h, 1% incline, then 2 min walk at 6.0 km/h. Repeat for 6 rounds, 42 min in total (about 6,240 steps).
4
Incline walk: 10 min at 6.0 km/h, 6% incline (about 1,200 steps).
5
Slow walk: 8 min at 4.5 km/h, 0% incline (about 800 steps). Total about 10,000 steps in 75 min.
6
Cycling option: 45–60 min on a stationary bike — 5 min easy warm-up, steady moderate pace at 75–90 RPM (or intervals), and 5 min cool-down.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Keep an easy, talkable effort — you should speak in short sentences while jogging or cycling.
📌Keep the incline at 1% when jogging and do not hold the handrails; set bike saddle height so the knee keeps a slight bend at the bottom.
⚠️Shin, knee, or foot pain that builds up means switch to walking or cycling for the day.
💡 Pro TipSteps are estimates (about 120 a minute walking, 160 jogging). Check your watch or phone and lengthen or shorten the final slow walk to land on 10,000. Cannot hold 9.0 km/h yet? Jog at 8.0 km/h and add a few minutes of walking.

UPPER DAY

01
Incline Bench Press Barbell / Dumbbell
Upper ChestFront DeltTriceps

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Set bench to 30–45°. Sit back with shoulder blades fully retracted and depressed into the pad.
2
Lower the barbell or dumbbells to your upper chest near the collarbone over 3 seconds.
3
Press upward smoothly to full extension above the shoulders and squeeze the upper chest.
4
Feel a controlled stretch in the upper chest at the bottom of every rep.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌30° hits upper chest best — 45° shifts more load toward the front deltoids.
📌Keep chest tall with feet planted firmly throughout the set.
⚠️Keep elbows angled ~45–60° — flaring wide increases shoulder strain.
💡 Pro TipDumbbell incline allows a deeper stretch — alternate with barbell incline weekly.
02
Lat Pulldown Wide (2s) + Close (2s)
LatsBicepsMid Back

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Wide Grip (2 sets): secure thighs under pads, grip bar wider than shoulder-width overhand, and lean back 10–15° with chest proud.
2
Depress shoulder blades first, pull bar to upper chest leading with elbows, then return slowly to a full stretch.
3
Close Grip (2 sets): switch to a V-bar or close underhand/neutral grip to target the lower lats and mid-back.
4
Pull to your upper sternum with elbows tucked close, pause 1 second at the bottom, and control the return.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Always pull to your chest, never behind the neck — behind-neck stresses the shoulders.
📌Wide grip emphasizes upper-lat width; close grip drives lower-lat sweep.
⚠️Don't swing your torso backward — keep a steady 10–15° lean.
💡 Pro TipThink "drive elbows into your back pockets" so your lats initiate the pull instead of your biceps.
03
Standing Military Barbell Press
All Deltoid HeadsTricepsCore

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Hold bar at collarbone height. Feet shoulder-width. Glutes and core fully squeezed.
2
Press bar overhead in slight arc around your face — not perfectly straight up.
3
Fully lock out arms overhead. Bar ends directly above your ears at lockout.
4
Lower with control to collarbone. Elbows stay under the bar throughout.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Core and glutes braced hard — prevents lower-back hyperextension.
📌Move your head slightly back as the bar passes, then push head "through the window" at lockout.
⚠️If your lower back arches excessively, reduce the weight immediately.
💡 Pro TipStanding version activates far more core and stabilizers vs seated — builds functional strength.
04
T-Bar Row Machine / Barbell
Mid Back ThicknessLats

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Set up on a chest-supported T-bar machine, or straddle a landmine barbell hinged forward at 45° with a flat back.
2
Drive elbows backward and pull the handle toward your lower chest/sternum.
3
Squeeze hard at the top for 1 second, pinching your shoulder blades together.
4
Extend arms under control on the return to get a full mid-back and lat stretch.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Prime builder for back thickness — pulldowns build width, T-bar rows build density.
📌Close V-handle targets mid-back/lats; wider pronated grip hits upper back & rear delts.
⚠️Don't jerk your torso upright — hold the hinge angle steady for the entire set.
💡 Pro TipUse chest-supported T-bar row if lower back fatigues — keeps form strict throughout.
05
Standing Machine Fly / Low-to-High Cable Crossover
ChestUpper ChestInner Chest Squeeze

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Standing Machine Fly: stand in a staggered stance with handles set just outside shoulder level, chest lifted, and elbows softly bent.
2
Low-to-High Cable Crossover: set dual pulleys low, step forward into a split stance, and start with palms angled forward and up.
3
Bring the handles together in front of your chest (or scoop upward to upper-chest height on cables) and squeeze hard for 1 second.
4
Open the arms back slowly to the start, keeping constant tension through the pecs and control through the full stretch.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Keep the sternum up, core tight, and shoulders packed down instead of shrugging or rolling forward.
📌Maintain the same soft elbow angle throughout the rep and think about bringing your biceps toward each other.
⚠️Do not let the weights pull your shoulders too far back — stay controlled in the stretch.
💡 Pro TipPause 1 second in the peak squeeze — standing machine fly maximizes mid-chest contraction, while low-to-high cables emphasize upper chest.
06
Lateral Raise Machine / Dumbbell
Side Deltoid

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Stand holding dumbbells at your sides with soft elbows, or sit in a lateral raise machine with elbows against the pads.
2
Raise both arms out in the scapular plane (slightly forward of your sides) to shoulder height.
3
Lead with your elbows and wrists level rather than shrugging your shoulders up.
4
Lower slowly over 3 seconds while keeping your upper traps relaxed.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Think "reach out toward the walls" rather than lifting straight up with your traps.
📌Keep shoulders depressed — shrugging shifts tension from side delts to traps.
⚠️Use controlled moderate weight — swinging heavy dumbbells steals work from the delts.
💡 Pro TipMachine lateral raises keep constant tension across the whole arc — alternate with dumbbells weekly.
07
Dumbbell / Barbell Curl
Biceps Brachii

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Stand tall holding dumbbells or a barbell with an underhand shoulder-width grip, arms fully extended.
2
Brace your core and keep elbows tucked at your sides throughout the set.
3
Curl the weight up by flexing the elbows only — no hip or lower-back swing.
4
Squeeze the biceps hard at the top (supinating palms up on dumbbells), then lower slowly.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Elbows stay pinned at your sides as the fixed pivot point.
📌Full supination on dumbbells maximizes biceps peak contraction.
⚠️Zero body swing — if your torso rocks, lower the weight.
💡 Pro TipEZ-bar or dumbbells are easier on the wrists — rotate with straight-bar curls across weeks.
08
Barbell Skull Crusher
Triceps Long Head + Lateral Head

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Lie on a flat bench holding a barbell or EZ-bar above your chest, arms straight and angled slightly back toward your head.
2
Lower the bar toward your forehead or just behind the crown of your head by bending only at the elbows.
3
Pause briefly at the bottom to feel a deep triceps long-head stretch.
4
Extend your arms back up and squeeze the triceps hard at the top.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Keep upper arms fixed and elbows tucked — don't let them flare wide.
📌Angling upper arms slightly back keeps tension on the triceps even at the top.
⚠️An EZ-bar reduces wrist strain compared to a straight barbell.
💡 Pro TipLowering slightly behind the head increases long-head stretch while being gentler on the elbows.

01
Bulgarian Split Squats
QuadsGlutesHamstringsBalance

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Stand about two feet in front of a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand. Rest the top of one foot on the bench behind you, laces down.
2
Set the front foot far enough forward that the knee stays above the ankle. Brace your core and keep your chest tall.
3
Lower straight down by bending the front knee until the front thigh is roughly parallel and the rear knee nears the floor.
4
Drive up through the front heel and squeeze the glute at the top. Finish all reps, then switch legs.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Keep your weight in the front heel — the back leg is only for balance.
📌Track the front knee over the foot and keep a tall torso with a slight forward lean.
⚠️Don't push off the back foot or let the front knee cave inward.
💡 Pro TipA longer stride emphasizes the glutes and hamstrings; a shorter, more upright stance shifts the load onto the quads.
02
Back Extension / Hyperextension
Lower BackGlutesHamstrings

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Set the hyperextension bench pad just below your hips and lock your feet under the ankle pads.
2
Cross your arms on your chest (or hold a plate) and hinge down at the hips with a flat back.
3
Squeeze your glutes and drive your torso up until it is in a straight line with your legs.
4
Pause at the top, then lower under control without rounding your lower back.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Drive the movement with glutes and hamstrings, not by arching the spine.
📌Stop at a straight line — do not over-extend past neutral.
⚠️Keep the neck neutral; don't throw the head back at the top.
💡 Pro TipHold the top for a second or hug a plate to build a stronger, more resilient lower back.
03
Seated Leg Curl
Hamstrings (Isolation)Knee Flexion

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Adjust the backrest so your knees align with the machine pivot, and set the ankle roller just above the back of your heels.
2
Lock the thigh pad snug over your lap above the knees to anchor your hips and thighs firmly.
3
Pull your toes toward your shins (dorsiflexion) and curl your heels as far under the seat as possible. Hold 1 second.
4
Return slowly over 3 seconds to a full hamstring stretch without letting the weight stack slam.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Sitting with flexed hips pre-stretches the hamstrings — superior for hamstring hypertrophy.
📌Keep the lap pad locked tight so your hips stay glued to the seat.
⚠️Directly trains knee flexion (including the biceps femoris short head that hip hinges miss).

Machine Adductor & Abductor

Adductor: sit in the machine with the pads on the inside of your thighs and your legs spread wide.

Squeeze your legs together against the pads, pause, then return slowly to a controlled stretch.

Barbell Calf Raise Stand (2s) + Sit (2s)
GastrocnemiusSoleus

Seated (2 sets — Soleus): sit on a bench with balls of your feet elevated and a padded barbell across your lower thighs (or use a seated calf machine).

Drop heels deep at the bottom, drive up to full tiptoe, hold 1 second, and complete 15–25 controlled reps.

📌Standing targets the gastrocnemius; seated (bent knee) isolates the deep soleus.

Core
06
Weighted Cable Crunches
Full AbsCore

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Kneel facing high cable. Hold rope ends at each side of your head.
2
Hips stay fixed and back — do NOT move them forward during the crunch.
3
Crunch torso DOWN toward your knees. Elbows drive toward thighs.
4
Squeeze abs hard at bottom. Return slowly. Hips stay back throughout.

📌Hips stay back — if hips move forward it becomes hip flexion, not a crunch.

07
Russian Twists
ObliquesCoreRotational Power

📋 Step by Step

1
Sit on floor with knees bent. Lean back to 45° — feel abs engage to hold position.
2
Lift feet slightly off the floor (harder) or keep them down (easier). Hold weight.
3
Rotate torso fully to the right, then fully to the left — one each side = one rep.
4
Control the rotation — don't just swing the weight. Feel each oblique contracting.

08
Plank with Shoulder Tap
Core StabilityAnti-Rotation

📸 Exercise Form

1
High plank: straight arms, body in perfect line from head to heels.
2
Feet slightly wider than usual to increase stability base significantly.
3
Lift one hand and tap opposite shoulder. Replace immediately. Alternate sides.
4
The goal: hips stay COMPLETELY still throughout every single tap.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Hips must not rotate or sway at all — resisting rotation is the entire goal.
📌Wider foot stance = easier. Progress by gradually narrowing the feet.
⚠️Core braced, glutes squeezed — keep the whole body tense like a rigid plank.
💡 Pro TipAnti-rotation training — directly transfers to heavier compound lifts and back health.

01
Cable Lateral Raise
Side Deltoid

📸 Exercise Form

1
Stand beside low cable. Grab handle with far hand, cable crossing body.

Slight elbow bend. Arm starts at hip — cable crosses in front of you.

02
Reverse Pec Fly
Rear DeltoidUpper BackPosture

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Set the pec-deck machine so the handles are in front of the shoulders and sit tall with the chest against the pad or torso supported.
2
Grab the handles with a slight bend in the elbows and pull the arms outward and backward in a wide arc.
3
Squeeze the rear delts and upper back when the arms reach shoulder line, keeping the neck relaxed and shoulders down.
4
Return slowly to the start without letting the plates slam, keeping tension on the rear delts throughout.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌 Keep the chest proud and spine neutral while the rear shoulders do the work.
📌 Think about spreading the handles apart rather than yanking with the hands.
⚠️ If your traps dominate or the elbows drop too low, reduce the load and reset your posture.
💡 Pro TipControl the return just as much as the squeeze — the eccentric phase is excellent for rear-delt growth.
03
Barbell Shrugs Forward (2s) + Backward (2s)
Upper TrapsNeck

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Forward Shrugs (2 sets): stand tall holding the barbell in front of your thighs with a shoulder-width overhand grip and straight arms.
2
Shrug shoulders straight up toward your ears, hold 1 second at the top, and lower slowly into a full stretch.
3
Backward Shrugs (2 sets): hold the barbell behind your glutes with arms straight and chest proud.
4
Elevate shoulders straight up and slightly back to squeeze the upper and middle traps, pause 1 second, and lower under control.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Forward/Backward refers to bar position (front vs behind-the-back), never rolling shoulders.
📌Move straight up and down on every rep with arms completely straight.
⚠️Avoid rolling the shoulders in circles — keep the head and neck neutral.
💡 Pro TipFront shrugs load the upper traps heavily, while behind-the-back shrugs emphasize posture and mid-trap retraction.
04
Cable Y Raise
Lower TrapsRear DeltsShoulder Stability

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Set cable pulleys low and hold one handle in each hand, or use a single low cable.
2
Start with arms slightly in front of the body and thumbs angled upward.
3
Raise the arms diagonally into a Y shape to about eye level.
4
Pause briefly, then lower slowly without shrugging.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Use very light weight and keep the neck relaxed.
📌Lead with the elbows and thumbs, not momentum.
⚠️Do not turn it into a front raise; keep the Y angle.
💡 Pro TipUseful for shoulder health and lower-trap activation after pressing and rowing.
05
Preacher Curl
Biceps Short HeadBrachialis

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Sit at preacher bench. Place upper arms flat on the angled pad — they stay there the whole set.
2
Hold EZ bar or dumbbells with underhand grip. Start at full arm extension for maximum stretch.
3
Curl upward by flexing elbows only. Squeeze hard at the top — hold 1 second.
4
Lower SLOWLY all the way back to full extension — the eccentric is where growth happens.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Upper arms stay flat on the pad the entire set — zero movement from them.
📌Emphasizes the short head and brachialis in a strict, cheat-free position.
⚠️Never drop the weight fast at the bottom — control the full eccentric stretch.
💡 Pro TipThe preacher pad eliminates all cheating — strict isolation you cannot get with standing curls.
06
Cable Rod Pushdown
Triceps Lateral & Medial Head

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Stand facing a high cable with a straight rod attachment. Grip it shoulder-width, elbows tucked at your sides.
2
Upper arms stay completely still — only the forearms move. Press the rod down to full extension.
3
Squeeze the triceps hard at the bottom with the arms fully straight.
4
Return slowly. The elbows must never drift forward away from your sides.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌A slight forward lean at the hips creates a better pressing angle for the triceps.
📌If the elbows drift up during the set, the weight is too heavy — reduce it.
⚠️Keep the wrists straight and stacked — don't let the bar bend them back.
💡 Pro TipSqueeze and hold one second at full extension — feel the horseshoe shape forming.
07
Reverse Grip Barbell Curl
Forearm ExtensorsBrachioradialis

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Stand tall holding a barbell or EZ-bar with a shoulder-width overhand grip — palms facing down throughout.
2
Pin elbows tight at your sides and keep wrists neutral — don't bend them forward or backward at all.
3
Curl upward as high as your grip allows and squeeze the forearm extensors and brachioradialis hard at the top.
4
Lower slowly to full extension. The extensor side fatigues fast — rest adequately between sets.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Barbell or EZ-bar keeps the pronated wrist angle consistent — targeting the brachioradialis effectively.
📌Targets brachioradialis and forearm extensors — the opposite side from regular underhand curls.
⚠️The extensor side is much weaker — go light initially and build load gradually with strict form.
💡 Pro TipBalanced forearms build upper-forearm thickness and help prevent tennis elbow and wrist pain during heavy lifting.
08
Barbell Wrist Curl + Wrist Extension
Forearm FlexorsForearm Extensors

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
WRIST CURL: Sit on bench, forearms on thighs, palms UP. Let weight roll to fingertips — full stretch. Curl wrists upward. 15–20 reps.
2
WRIST EXTENSION: Flip palms DOWN. Let wrists drop fully — feel extensor stretch. Extend the backs of your hands upward against gravity. 15–20 reps.
3
Perform both movements back to back as a superset for maximum forearm pump.
4
Use light weight only — forearm tendons are easily irritated with heavy loads.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Forearms stay flat on thighs — only wrists move throughout both exercises.
📌Training both sides builds complete, balanced forearm development.
⚠️Never force range of motion on extensions — extensor tendons irritate easily.
💡 Pro TipDoing both flexion and extension every session prevents forearm imbalances and elbow pain.
Treadmill / Cycling · 10,000 steps
09
Treadmill / Cycling · Walk + Incline + Jog
WalkIncline WalkJogCycling10,000 steps75 min

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Warm-up walk: 5 min at 6.0 km/h, 0% incline (about 600 steps).
2
Incline walk: 10 min at 6.0 km/h, 6% incline (about 1,200 steps).
3
Jog and walk: 5 min jog at 9.0 km/h, 1% incline, then 2 min walk at 6.0 km/h. Repeat for 6 rounds, 42 min in total (about 6,240 steps).
4
Incline walk: 10 min at 6.0 km/h, 6% incline (about 1,200 steps).
5
Slow walk: 8 min at 4.5 km/h, 0% incline (about 800 steps). Total about 10,000 steps in 75 min.
6
Cycling option: 45–60 min on a stationary bike — 5 min easy warm-up, steady moderate pace at 75–90 RPM (or intervals), and 5 min cool-down.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Keep an easy, talkable effort — you should speak in short sentences while jogging or cycling.
📌Keep the incline at 1% when jogging and do not hold the handrails; set bike saddle height so the knee keeps a slight bend at the bottom.
⚠️Shin, knee, or foot pain that builds up means switch to walking or cycling for the day.
💡 Pro TipSteps are estimates (about 120 a minute walking, 160 jogging). Check your watch or phone and lengthen or shorten the final slow walk to land on 10,000. Cannot hold 9.0 km/h yet? Jog at 8.0 km/h and add a few minutes of walking.

01
Deep Lunges
Hip FlexorsQuads20–30 sec per side

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Step one foot far forward into a lunge position.
2
Sink your hips down and forward until you feel a stretch at the front of the back hip.
3
Keep the chest tall and the front knee over the ankle.
4
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Squeeze the glute of the back leg to deepen the stretch.
📌Keep the torso upright and the ribs down.
⚠️Do not let the front knee collapse inward.
💡 Pro TipOpens the hip flexors tightened by squats, lunges and sitting.
02
World’s Greatest Stretch
HipsHamstringsUpper Back3 per side

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
From a deep lunge, place both hands on the floor inside the front foot.
2
Sink the hips low and press the front knee gently out against the elbow.
3
Rotate your chest toward the front knee and reach that arm to the ceiling.
4
Hold briefly, return the hand to the floor, and repeat 3 times per side.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Follow your top hand with your eyes as you rotate.
📌Keep the back leg long and the hips low.
⚠️Move slowly and breathe through each rotation.
💡 Pro TipOne movement that stretches hips, hamstrings and the upper back together.
03
Calf Stretch
CalvesAchilles30 sec per side

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Stand facing a wall with one foot forward and one foot back.
2
Keep the back leg straight with the heel flat on the floor.
3
Lean toward the wall until you feel a stretch in the back calf.
4
Hold 30 seconds, then switch legs.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Keep the back heel pressed into the floor.
📌Point both feet straight ahead.
⚠️Do not bounce — hold the stretch steady.
💡 Pro TipBend the back knee slightly to reach the lower calf and Achilles.
04
Tibialis Stretch
Tibialis AnteriorShins30 sec per side

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Stand on one leg and place the top of the other foot on the floor behind you, toes pointing back.
2
Bend the standing knee slightly so the front of the shin stretches.
3
Gently press the foot into the floor without rolling the ankle.
4
Hold 30 seconds, then switch legs.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Keep the pressure gentle and even across the top of the foot.
📌Hold a wall or rack for balance.
⚠️Ease off if you feel a pinch at the front of the ankle.
💡 Pro TipBest after Legs + Core Day, when the shins have been trained.
05
Single-Leg Glute Stretch
GlutesHip Rotators30 sec per side

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Lie on your back with both legs extended on the floor.
2
Bend one knee and hug it toward your chest with both hands.
3
Keep the other leg long and relaxed on the floor, with the lower back flat.
4
Hold 30 seconds, then switch sides.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Keep the head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.
📌Draw the knee gently toward your chest or slightly across toward the opposite shoulder to feel it in the glute.
⚠️Stop if you feel pinching in the hip joint instead of a stretch in the glute.
💡 Pro TipHelpful after squats, lunges and deadlifts.
06
Single-Leg Hamstring Stretch
HamstringsCalves30 sec per side

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Sit on the floor with one leg extended straight and the other knee bent out to the side.
2
Hinge forward from the hips, keeping the back long.
3
Reach both hands toward the extended foot until you feel the back of the thigh stretch.
4
Hold 30 seconds, then switch legs.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Lead with the chest, not the head.
📌Keep the extended foot relaxed with the toes pointing up.
⚠️Do not force the leg flat or round the back to reach further.
💡 Pro TipBreathe out slowly to relax deeper into the stretch.
07
Seated Toe Touch
HamstringsLower Back30 sec hold

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Sit on the floor with both legs extended in front of you.
2
Hinge forward from the hips, keeping the back long.
3
Reach toward your toes as far as is comfortable.
4
Hold 30 seconds while breathing slowly.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Lead with the chest, not the head.
📌Keep the knees soft if the hamstrings are tight.
⚠️Do not force a rounded back to reach the toes.
💡 Pro TipReach for the shins first — flexibility builds with consistency.
08
Single-Leg Seated Toe Touch
HamstringsCalves30 sec per side

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Sit with one leg extended and the other knee bent with the foot against the inner thigh.
2
Hinge forward from the hips toward the extended foot.
3
Reach for your toes keeping the back long, not rounded.
4
Hold 30 seconds, then switch sides.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Keep the extended leg relaxed with the toes up.
📌Hinge from the hips, not the upper back.
⚠️Stay in the stretch without bouncing.
💡 Pro TipDoing one leg at a time shows any left-right tightness.
09
Butterfly Pose
AdductorsHips30 sec hold

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Sit tall and bring the soles of your feet together with the knees dropped out to the sides.
2
Hold your feet or ankles and keep the spine long.
3
Hinge slightly forward from the hips for a deeper stretch.
4
Hold 30 seconds while breathing slowly.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Sit on a folded towel if the hips feel tight.
📌Let gravity lower the knees — do not push them down.
⚠️Stop if you feel pressure in the knees.
💡 Pro TipA good stretch for the inner thighs and hips.
10
Cobra Pose
AbsSpineHip Flexors20–30 sec hold

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Lie face-down with your hands under your shoulders and legs extended.
2
Press through your hands and lift your chest off the floor.
3
Keep the hips on the floor and the shoulders away from your ears.
4
Hold 20–30 seconds, then lower slowly.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Lift through the chest and keep the neck long.
📌Keep the glutes relaxed and the legs resting on the floor.
⚠️Ease off if you feel pinching in the lower back.
💡 Pro TipOpens the abs and hip flexors after core and leg work.
11
Cat-Cow Pose
SpineCore10 slow reps

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Start on hands and knees with the wrists under the shoulders and knees under the hips.
2
Cow: inhale, drop the belly and lift the chest and tailbone.
3
Cat: exhale, round the spine toward the ceiling and tuck the chin.
4
Flow slowly between both shapes for 10 reps.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Move with your breath — slow and smooth.
📌Keep the arms straight and the shoulders away from the ears.
⚠️Do not force the end range of either position.
💡 Pro TipA gentle way to release the spine after heavy lifting.
12
Child’s Pose
Lower BackLatsHips30–60 sec hold

📸 Exercise Form

📋 Step by Step

1
Kneel on the floor with the big toes touching and the knees apart.
2
Sit your hips back toward your heels.
3
Walk your hands forward and rest your forehead on the floor.
4
Breathe slowly and hold 30–60 seconds.

🎯 Posture Cues

📌Let the lower back relax and lengthen with each breath.
📌Reach your arms long to stretch the lats.
⚠️Place a cushion under the knees or hips if they feel uncomfortable.
💡 Pro TipFinish here to bring your heart rate down and relax.
